documents.title: Rheumatology annual follow-up
documents.author: rheumatology
documents.body:
Rheumatology — annual visit 1/26/2026

Seropositive erosive RA on hydroxychloroquine 300 mg daily since 11/2023. No flares this year. Morning stiffness minimal. Working full time without limitation.

Other: PBC on ursodiol with good response; central hypothyroidism diagnosed by endocrinology last summer, levothyroxine now 137 mcg.

Exam: no synovitis, no nodules, full grip both hands.

Assessment: RA in sustained low disease activity on hydroxychloroquine.
Plan: continue. Eye screening per ophthalmology schedule. Return in one year.

Rheumatology

orders.order: MRI brain with and without contrast

documents.title: Office Visit — Headaches and Visual Difficulty
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
S: Two problems that she now thinks go together. (1) Dull, pressure-like headaches, frontal, that have been getting steadily worse over the past few months. (2) She keeps bumping into things — walked into a door frame at work last week, catches her hip on furniture at home. Says things "come out of nowhere" from the sides. Also: no period for about a year now. No hot flashes or sweats.

Meds: levothyroxine 137 mcg, ursodiol 500 mg BID, hydroxychloroquine 300 mg daily, topical steroids PRN.
NKDA.

O: BP and pulse normal, afebrile. Alert, appropriate. Acuity grossly normal with near card both eyes. Confrontation fields: reduced in the temporal fields of both eyes. Pupils equal and reactive. Fundi difficult undilated; discs look sharp where seen. EOMs full. Face symmetric. Strength, sensation, reflexes, gait normal. Neck supple.

A: Progressive headaches with bilateral temporal field loss and a year of amenorrhea in a woman with central hypothyroidism. Needs urgent imaging of the brain and sella.

P:
- MRI brain with and without contrast, marked urgent; staff to get the earliest slot.
- Messaged her endocrinologist; her overdue follow-up there will be moved up.
- Return or ED for sudden severe headache, double vision or sudden vision loss.

reports.study: MRI brain with and without contrast
reports.text:
Indication: progressive headaches, bitemporal visual field loss, amenorrhea.
Technique: multiplanar multisequence MRI of the brain before and after IV gadolinium, with thin-section coronal and sagittal imaging through the sella.
Findings: There is a 2.5 cm enhancing sellar and suprasellar mass, measured in craniocaudal dimension on coronal post-contrast images, extending upward from an expanded sella and compressing adjacent structures. The normal pituitary gland is not separately identified. No hemorrhage within the mass. The brain parenchyma is otherwise normal without mass effect elsewhere, hydrocephalus or abnormal enhancement. Ventricles normal in size. Major intracranial flow voids preserved.
reports.conclusion: 2.5 cm suprasellar mass compressing adjacent structures, most consistent with a pituitary macroadenoma. Endocrine correlation recommended.

documents.title: Endocrinology visit — pituitary mass
documents.author: endocrinology
documents.body:
Endocrinology — clinic note, 7/20/2026

Ms. Winslow returns, brought forward after her primary care physician's MRI. History: Graves' disease treated with radioactive iodine about ten years ago, longstanding hypothyroidism, and central hypothyroidism diagnosed here last summer.

In her words, "I keep walking into furniture and door frames." She has dull, pressure-type headaches that have worsened over recent months. Her last menstrual period was about a year ago; before that she cycled regularly every 25-30 days, bleeding 3-4 days. She has had no hot flashes or night sweats.

Medications: levothyroxine 137 mcg daily, ursodiol 500 mg twice daily, hydroxychloroquine 300 mg daily.
Allergies: NKDA.
Family: father died of colon cancer at 65.
Social: never smoker, no alcohol, administrative assistant.

BP 130/78, HR 72, BMI 29 kg/m2.
Visual acuity 20/20 in each eye. Neurological examination otherwise normal. Breast examination: on palpation of the areola, milky discharge expressed bilaterally.

MRI 7/16 reviewed: 2.5 cm suprasellar mass compressing adjacent structures.

Impression: pituitary macroadenoma with galactorrhea and amenorrhea; a prolactinoma is the leading possibility. The bitemporal field loss needs formal measurement.

Plan:
- Prolactin (lab asked to run serial dilutions to avoid a hook effect), LH, FSH, free T4 today; 8 AM cortisol tomorrow morning.
- Formal visual fields with ophthalmology this month.
- I will call her with results and start treatment as indicated.

Endocrinology

documents.title: Endocrinology results letter — prolactinoma
documents.author: endocrinology
documents.body:
Endocrinology — results and plan, 7/22/2026

Dear Doctor,

Results:
  Prolactin 2,140 ng/mL (after dilution)
  LH 1.1 mIU/mL, FSH 2.6 mIU/mL — inappropriately low for her age and amenorrhea
  Free T4 1.1 ng/dL on levothyroxine 137 mcg
  8 AM cortisol 13.6 mcg/dL — adequate; no steroid cover needed

A prolactin of this magnitude with a 2.5 cm sellar/suprasellar mass is diagnostic of a macroprolactinoma. It accounts for the galactorrhea and amenorrhea, the low gonadotropins, and in all likelihood the central hypothyroidism.

Treatment is medical first, even with field loss; dopamine agonists usually shrink these tumors and visual fields often improve within weeks.

Plan:
1. Cabergoline 0.25 mg twice weekly, increasing to 0.5 mg twice weekly in two weeks if tolerated. Take with food at bedtime to limit nausea and lightheadedness.
2. Humphrey visual fields with ophthalmology 7/29.
3. Prolactin again in 4-5 weeks (order sent to your lab for convenience).
4. Repeat pituitary MRI in about 3 months.
5. Continue levothyroxine 137 mcg.
6. She should seek care immediately for sudden severe headache or sudden change in vision.

I spoke with her at length by phone this morning.

Endocrinology

documents.title: Ophthalmology — visual field assessment
documents.author: ophthalmology
documents.body:
Neuro-ophthalmic assessment, 7/29/2026
Referred by endocrinology: 2.5 cm pituitary macroadenoma (prolactinoma), cabergoline started 7/22.

VA 20/20 OD, 20/20 OS. Pupils equal, no RAPD. Color vision full both eyes. IOP normal. Anterior segments quiet.
Dilated exam: optic discs pink and well-perfused without pallor, healthy rims. Maculae normal. No hydroxychloroquine changes.
Humphrey 24-2 SITA: reliable both eyes. Dense temporal hemifield defects in each eye respecting the vertical meridian — bitemporal hemianopia.

Impression: bitemporal hemianopia, in keeping with the known pituitary macroadenoma. No optic atrophy.
Plan: repeat fields in 6-8 weeks on cabergoline. Same-day contact for any sudden vision change.

Ophthalmology

Two weeks on cabergoline 0.25 mg twice weekly. Taking it at bedtime with a snack and tolerating it. Increasing to 0.5 mg twice weekly as planned (1 whole tablet). Ophthalmology fields 7/29 confirmed bitemporal hemianopia; repeat in 6-8 weeks. Prolactin due around 8/24 at primary care's lab.
